objections.claim: External-state isolation remains optional and therefore does not establish discrimination. Fresh TMPDIR/HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME values do not prevent an oracle from using absolute shared paths such as /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, or a writable workspace sibling; the only stated confinement is bwrap “where available.” Without bwrap, an input-ignoring oracle can create a marker during baseline and observe it during the negative run, yielding the required 0/nonzero pair without inspecting the mutation. This defeats the promised external-marker regression and leaves frozen governance correction d unresolved. Confinement must be mandatory with fail-closed oracle-unrunnable behavior when unavailable, or an equivalent mechanism must prove no mutable state is shared. Candidate artifact: sha256:a362a8eeea18d2a0af48d4dc463ef6a115e4237f0d02ab7d3a867d1d8d92da35.

The credential requirements are mutually unsatisfiable. E1 requires the merge controller to use a repository-writing principal that is explicitly non-admin and non-bypass, and the branch publisher also holds a non-bypass write credential. E2 and the release design simultaneously require custody-drift to reject every repository-writing credential beyond the recorded writer set, stated as “the Eye alone.” A non-Eye controller/publisher principal therefore makes every authority/release ceremony fail custody-drift; using the Eye’s credential instead violates E1’s non-admin condition and gives the publisher/controller the Eye-only tag/release capability. The approach needs an explicit capability-bounded writer lifecycle or revocation/ceremony mechanism that makes E1 operable while preserving the closed release-writer invariant, with regressions covering both states. Candidate artifact: sha256:a362a8eeea18d2a0af48d4dc463ef6a115e4237f0d02ab7d3a867d1d8d92da35.
